subject: POC evaluation plan, success criteria & shadowing approach (next steps)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2025 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: POC evaluation plan, success criteria & shadowing approach (next steps)

Hi Dana — thanks again for a productive discovery earlier. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan for your review so we can get the trial scheduled next week. Please confirm or flag changes by EOD Tue so we can lock dates.

Recap (from today’s call)
- Goal: validate Redwood serving for Acme support assistant (latency, quality, safety) with live traffic shadow for 2 weeks, plus offline evals on historical dialogs.
- Primary success criteria you prioritized:
  - Accuracy/utility: >= 85% pass rate on your rubric (see attached template)
  - Safety: zero high-severity policy violations detected by your safety tests
  - Latency: P95 token turnaround < 350ms for 2k-concurrent sessions simulated
  - Cost: baseline token cost < $0.003/token (target) during shadow run

Proposed evaluation plan
1) Offline evals (week 0–1):
   - We (Redwood) run model outputs against a curated set of ~500 historical tickets you shared (anonymized) and grade with your rubric.
   - Deliverable: offline eval report with per-metric pass/fail and sample failure cases.
2) Shadow run (weeks 2–3):
   - Live traffic mirrored to Redwood (read-only) behind a feature flag; we do not surface answers to customers.
   - Real-time telemetry: latency, token counts, safety events. We run A/B comparison vs your current system on matched sessions.
3) Pilot (optional week 4):
   - Canary responses to 5% of traffic with human-in-the-loop review before full production.

Owners & timelines
- Redwood: Jasmine (eng + sales coordination), Neha (integration lead, infra & safety), Marcus (performance lead)
- Acme: Dana (product sponsor), +security@acme.com for SOC2 needs
- Proposed kickoff: Nov 11 (integration prep Nov 3–9)

Attachments included: acme-poc-eval-template.xlsx (rubric + scoring), redwood-shadow-runbook.pdf (ops checklist).

Ask / next steps
- Dana: confirm success criteria and the two-week shadow cadence, and whether we can get the anonymized historical dataset by Nov 6.
- Security: if SOC2 evidence is needed, please point us to the contact and we’ll share the checklist.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a HubSpot sequence and a short SOW doc for signatures once you confirm.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.com]

If we can get responses on 1–3 by Wed, Nov 5 we’ll be able to commit to the Nov 11 kickoff.

Jasmine / team — following up with specifics to respond to Acme’s questions and to lock internal owners.

1) Data handling & privacy - We will accept an anonymized export. Redwood supports on-the-fly PII hashing and we can enable a filter to drop or mask any fields flagged by Acme. We do not persist customer identifiers in analytics or logs by default; any persistent debug artifacts are sanitized and stored in a customer-scoped bucket with restricted IAM. We can provide the exact KMS key ID and retention window for the POC upon request.

2) Shadow access pattern - For the shadow run we’ll request a mirror endpoint (read-only) and deploy a transient ingestion worker that forwards traffic to the inference cluster. No writeback will be enabled. We log request metadata (latency, tokens, safety flags) but strip identifying fields before storage.

3) Token accounting / telemetry - Reporting cadence: daily summary + final POC report. Granularity: per-route aggregates and per-hour P95/P99 latency slices; we’ll include token counts per-session in anonymized buckets. CSV export provided.

4) Offline eval rubric (quick outline)
- Dataset: ~500 tickets sampled across channels.
- Grading scale per sample: 0 = unacceptable, 1 = partially helpful, 2 = fully helpful.
- Pass threshold: average score >= 1.7 (equates to ~85% pass).
- Failure analysis: top 10 failure types with recommended remediation (prompting, system messages, or model variant).

5) Performance targets & smoke tests - Marcus will own load test scenarios. Baseline P95 target: <350ms; fail if sustained >500ms for >5% of windows. Marcus will run an initial sim by Nov 7 and share the report.

6) Kickoff & SOW - Proposed kickoff remains Nov 11. I’ll prepare an integration checklist (internal) and Jasmine can send the SOW. We should also include a short Zoom for the engineering priming session on Nov 11.

I’ve also added two deliverables to the HubSpot deal (links below).

-Neha
